Review target: rrnewton/reverie, https://github.com/rrnewton/reverie/pull/625, dc7dac97995fee2393d2bcef147116134314781a..03ce6d472df1537b68fdc6ead5e2a89d5294a390

Artifact identity: verified.
- HEAD is 03ce6d472df1537b68fdc6ead5e2a89d5294a390 and its parent is dc7dac97995fee2393d2bcef147116134314781a.
- `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no` printed nothing, so the tracked tree is clean.
- SHA-256 of `git diff <base> <head>` is a16c40b0b4974135f6fa05399a75392e9ab1ec03360611d71110d8f8d4480ee6, matching the expected value.
- `cmp` against `ignored/recovery/read-pread-lowword-20260923/read-pread-lowword-frozen-v1.diff` returned 0 (byte-identical).
- The diff touches 2 files, with 239 lines added and 6 removed. The 6 removed lines are exactly the two 3-line `i32::try_from(args[0])` guards.

Findings:
I found no correctness defect or regression against the stated claim. The items below are low-severity or informational and do not block this PR.
- Low (older than this PR; aliased descriptors now inherit it): reverie-kvm/src/executor.rs:5716–5735 — scalar `pread64` on a non-fdinfo descriptor never checks for a negative offset itself.
  - EINVAL comes back only from the host `read_at` call at 5735. That runs after the descriptor lookup (5716), the zero-length return (5722) and the buffer check (5725). Linux `ksys_pread64` rejects `pos < 0` before it looks up the descriptor.
  - Where results differ from Linux (which returns EINVAL in all three cases):
    - bad descriptor with offset −1: EBADF;
    - good descriptor with offset −1 and a bad buffer: EFAULT;
    - good descriptor with length 0 and offset −1: 0.
  - For an aliased descriptor, that last case returned EBADF at base and returns 0 at head. Both differ from Linux; head now matches the plain descriptor, which is exactly what the PR claims.
  - Other paths already get this right: `pwrite64` (5745) and `vectored_io` (6258–6298) check the offset before the descriptor lookup, and the fdinfo `read` (1805–1833) checks it before the buffer.
  - Required change: none for this PR. A follow-up should move the check to the top, as `pwrite64` does.
- Low (older than this PR): reverie-kvm/src/executor.rs:5722–5727 — `pread64` on a pipe or socket returns 0 for length 0 and EFAULT for a bad buffer. Linux returns ESPIPE, because its FMODE_PREAD check comes before `vfs_read`; here ESPIPE only comes from the host `read_at`. Required change: none here; follow-up.
- Low (older than this PR): reverie-kvm/src/executor.rs:5690 and 5719 — `ensure_readable` returns EISDIR (5258–5259) before the buffer check (5697 and 5725). A directory with a bad buffer therefore gets EISDIR, where Linux `vfs_read` runs `access_ok` before the directory's read handler and returns EFAULT. Required change: none here; follow-up.
- Informational (test coverage): reverie-kvm/src/executor.rs:33783–33894 and reverie-kvm/tests/static_elf.rs:16144–16264 — both new tests alias only regular-file descriptors.
  - These alias paths are untested:
    - stdin (5669–5683): `HIGH_WORD|0` returned EBADF at base and now reads stdin, as on Linux;
    - the fdinfo route (5662, 5709);
    - `signalfd_read` (5694);
    - random-device descriptors;
    - Host thread-ownership mode, where reads are backend-owned (runtime.rs:5336).
  - By reading the code, all of these are correct. Each function decodes the descriptor once and every branch uses that value. Every executor entry point passes the raw request through unchanged (runtime.rs:488, 699, 1461, 4113, 5561).
  - Suggested follow-up: add a stdin alias case. It is not required for this claim.
- Informational: executor.rs:33874, 33884 and static_elf.rs:16198, 16201 — the bit-31 cases return EBADF under both the old and new decoders, so they cannot tell the two apart. They do catch a future decoder that drops bit 31.
  - EBADF is guaranteed because no negative key can exist in the descriptor tables.
  - Every production insertion into `state.files` and `state.fdinfo_files` takes a descriptor from `0..GUEST_NOFILE_LIMIT` (executor.rs:7815, 7939–7943, 8023, 10457); 2093 reuses a descriptor that was already allocated.
  - `is_open_standard` only accepts descriptors 0–2 (13492).

Goalpost-moving assessment:
- Assertions weakened: no — the diff edits no existing test.
  - Both test hunks are pure additions: executor.rs `@@ -33782,6 +33780,119 @@` adds 113 lines, and static_elf.rs `@@ -16141,5 +16141,127 @@` adds 122.
  - The 2-line shift in the executor.rs hunk comes from the two production hunks above it.
- Tolerance widened, exemption added, case skipped, or comparator relaxed: no — no threshold, allowlist, skip or comparator was changed.
  - The KVM test requires stdout and stderr to be byte-identical to the native run and the exit code to be exactly 0. It checks this over 4 runs: 2 direct and 2 Tool-owned.
  - The native run itself must exit 0, print exactly `read-pread-low-word-ok\n` and leave stderr empty.
  - The test's only skip is the existing `kvm_available` helper (static_elf.rs:4105–4117), which returns early unless `REVERIE_REQUIRE_KVM` is set. This PR did not add it, and I ran with `REVERIE_REQUIRE_KVM=1`.
- Failure renamed or relabelled as a pass: no — no label, classification or expected-failure marker was touched.
- Check deleted instead of satisfied: no.
  - The removed guards (base executor.rs:5660–5662 and 5708–5710) rejected any nonzero high word. That is the non-Linux behaviour being fixed.
  - The part Linux requires — EBADF for a low word ≥ 2^31, returned before the buffer is checked — is still enforced by the guaranteed lookup miss described above.
  - New bit-31 cases in both tests now assert it; base had no test for it.

Residual risks:
1. Scalar `pread64` still orders its errors differently from Linux (negative offset, ESPIPE), and so do `read`/`pread64` on directories (EISDIR instead of EFAULT). These predate the PR, and aliased descriptors now inherit them.
2. Alias behaviour on stdin, fdinfo, signalfd and random-device descriptors, and in Host thread-ownership mode, is verified by reading the code only.
3. Other syscalls still use the strict decoder, so they return EBADF for high-word aliases that Linux accepts. This is outside this PR. The sites are:
   - sendfile `out_fd` (executor.rs:6533);
   - lseek (6749);
   - sendto (10045) and recvfrom (10101);
   - fstatfs (11905);
   - fchdir (12623);
   - getdents64 (13436);
   - the f*xattr family (14161);
   - the non-write branch of `virtual_signalfd_write_error` (7884);
   - one site at 11453 that I did not identify.
4. The tests do not cover replay, record, log or L2 parity, and the PR does not claim them.
5. I did not run the tests at base, because the checkout could not be changed. The claim that they would fail on the old decoder rests on reasoning: every alias returns EBADF there, so the unit test fails at its first assertion (33799, which expects EFAULT) and the guest exits 3 in all four KVM runs.
6. Both tests ran from existing binaries; cargo recompiled nothing.
   - That relies on cargo's timestamp check: `executor.rs` was last modified at 00:21:36, before the library test binary was built at 00:22:00. `static_elf.rs` was last modified at 00:19:03, before the static_elf binary was built at 00:26:09.
   - The tracked tree is clean at head.
   - A pass is only possible if the linked library decodes the low word.
7. On a host without KVM, or with `REVERIE_REQUIRE_KVM` unset, the KVM test passes silently. This behaviour already existed. CI evidence for this test must show the variable was set, or show guest output.

Verification:
- Identity: `git rev-parse HEAD` and `HEAD^`, `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no` (empty), `sha256sum` of the `git diff <base> <head>` output, and `cmp` against the frozen artifact (rc=0).
- Unit test: `cargo test --offline -p reverie-kvm --lib -- --exact executor::tests::read_and_pread64_consume_low_descriptor_words`
  - Result: rc=0, `1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 815 filtered out; finished in 0.01s`, 0.132 s wall clock.
  - Binary: `target/debug/deps/reverie_kvm-543bfc99885654c3`.
- KVM test: `env REVERIE_REQUIRE_KVM=1 cargo test --offline -p reverie-kvm --test static_elf -- --exact read_and_pread64_consume_low_descriptor_words_on_kvm --nocapture`
  - Result: rc=0, captured before the output was read. `1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 340 filtered out; finished in 0.26s`, 0.377 s wall clock.
  - Binary: `target/debug/deps/static_elf-631e2c0a95c3bdc8`. The log has 0 "skipping" lines.
  - The two Tool-owned runs (`guest-read-pread-low-word-true-0` and `-true-1`) printed 100 `[kvm-strace]` lines, including:
    - `pread64(3, 0xfffecee, 2, 2) = 2`
    - `lseek(3, 0, SEEK_CUR) = 2`
    - `read(3, 0xffffffffffffffff, 1) = -14`
    - `pread64(3, 0xfffecee, 1, -1) = -22`
    - `read(-2147483645, 0xffffffffffffffff, 1) = -9`
  - StraceTool prints the typed, low-word view of the descriptor; the executor received the raw aliased word through `inject`. These lines go to host stderr, not to the guest stderr the test compares.
  - The native run passing also confirms, on this host's kernel (Linux 7.1.3), that aliased descriptors are accepted and bit-31 values return EBADF.
- Code traced:
  - executor.rs: dispatch (430–516), `read`/`pread64` (5659–5742), `pwrite64` (5744–5749), fdinfo `read` (1805–1833), routing classifiers (3549–3587), `execute_checked`/`execute` (5104–5209), `is_open_standard` (13491–13496), descriptor allocation (2084–2114, 7809–7834, 7930–8100, 10452–10466), `insert_file` (elf.rs:873);
  - runtime.rs: routing (5328–5342, 5557–5563), `inject` (1436–1522), executor wrappers (487–489, 663–703), polled-read site (821–834);
  - `typed_syscall!` raw arguments (reverie-syscalls macros.rs:69–101);
  - the 64-bit `rdi` store in the trampoline (bootstrap.rs:784–864);
  - StraceTool (tools.rs:113–148);
  - `run_static_elf_captured` (vm.rs:4218–4369).
- Limitations:
  - The Linux ordering I compared against is upstream `fs/read_write.c` (`ksys_read`, `vfs_read`, `ksys_pread64`) from my own knowledge; I did not consult a kernel tree.
  - Error-ordering combinations the tests don't cover were not run natively.
  - I did not look at GitHub or CI, which the brief prohibited, and did not run broader suites, which were out of scope.
  - The Meta `search_files` tool failed ("'git' is not a known Biggrep repository"), so I used Grep limited to reverie-kvm/src, reverie-kvm/tests and reverie-syscalls/src.
- Environment: `/dev/kvm` is `crw-rw-rw-`; 316 cores, load average about 30; cargo 1.99.0-nightly (3efb1f477 2026-07-17); rustc 1.99.0-nightly (26ae60a9e 2026-07-28).

Verdict: approve, bound to exact head 03ce6d472df1537b68fdc6ead5e2a89d5294a390 (diff SHA-256 a16c40b0b4974135f6fa05399a75392e9ab1ec03360611d71110d8f8d4480ee6). Any new head needs a fresh review.

I made no changes to the checkout. Outside it, I added one memory note (`kvm-test-evidence-require-kvm.md`, indexed in `MEMORY.md`): KVM test evidence should be run with `REVERIE_REQUIRE_KVM=1` and show the guest actually ran.
